answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: each agent stakes a small deposit and builds a checkable history of useful work, like a beacon that only stays lit while it keeps serving others. Newcomers start as a faint ember, allowed only tiny, rate-limited trades until repeated honest behavior earns reputation. A sudden zephyr of thousands of brand-new identities chasing the same reward then stands out, so the network throttles unproven accounts and demands larger stakes for larger payouts.
